en.title: Number of Subsequences Lexicographically Greater Than the System Password
en.description:
Among all index subsequences of customer, count those that are lexicographically strictly greater than system. Identical strings chosen from different indices are counted separately; when system is a prefix, the longer string is greater. Output the result modulo 10⁹+7.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O and judging; ranges marked as this site's are not original source constraints.
en.input: Two lines with the lowercase strings customer and system, of lengths 1..100000 and 1..100 respectively.
en.explanation: Example 1: the two b at different indices, plus ba, bb, bab, 5 in total. Example 2: only aa is greater than a; the two single a are equal, so the answer is 1. Example 3: a is smaller than z, so there is no qualifying subsequence, and the answer is 0.
hints: dp[j] records the number of subsequences exactly equal to the first j characters of system, and greater records the number already greater. Each new character doubles greater; an equal prefix followed by a larger character, or the complete system followed by any character, also becomes greater; update the equal-prefix DP in reverse order.
